text:
maya: Quick pulse — APAC demand forecast for embeddings/chat endpoints bumped ~12% for Oct–Dec. H200 lead times from our usual suppliers are hitting 10–14 weeks in APAC. Need a short plan: reservations vs fallbacks (H100/L40S), short-term buffer, and action owners.

simon: Can you share the projected GPU hours so we can map to node reservations?

dinesh: Baseline we used in Q3 planning was ~8000 GPU-hours/day across APAC clusters. With +12% seasonal, peak ~8960 GPU-hours/day. Rough throughput estimates: H200 ~= 1.4x H100 for our mixed quantized configs; L40S gives good cost/throughput for short bursts.

ashley: Initial proposal: reserve ~60% of incremental demand on Dedicated H200 (committed), keep ~25% as L40S burst/spot capacity for tails, and leave ~15% to H100 fallback or cross-region spill. That hedges lead-time risk while containing costs.

simon: Region split details? we should avoid assuming uniform availability.

dinesh: Vendor quotes: SG ~14 weeks for new H200 orders, JP/SYD ~10–12 weeks. L40S availability is much better (2–4 weeks) and can be used as a stopgap. Also need to watch freight/assembly delays — quoted delivery windows are optimistic.

maya: Cost note: H200 is ~2.2x H100 on list price/hour but because throughput is higher, cost per effective token/latency-SLO can be better for low-latency routes. Still, committing all-in to H200 raises cash and lead-time exposure.

ashley: Action items (proposal):
1) Procurement to open POs for H200 reserve for JP+SG by end of Tues (target coverage = 60% incremental).
2) Infra to provision an L40S burst pool + BGP/routing policy to prefer local H200, fallback to L40S within the 50ms SLA window.
3) Scheduling/platform team to run a failover dry-run next Wed simulating H200 shortage and validate KV-cache / batching behavior under L40S.

simon: I'll add a canary routing rule: prefer H200 for latency-sensitive routes, route to L40S when tail latency > threshold or queue depth > X. Keep rollout gated.

infra-bot: Created capacity ticket CAP-2026-APAC-H200-01, assigned to @dinesh and @ashley. Estimated delivery window added to ticket.

dinesh: Quick calc snippet for visibility:
```
# quick calc (approx)
baseline = 8000  # gpu-hours/day
seasonal = 0.12
peak = baseline * (1 + seasonal)  # ~8960 gpu-hours/day
reserve_pct = 0.6
h200_monthly_hours = peak * reserve_pct * 30  # ~161280 GPU-hours/month
# node-hours: if an H200 node provides ~24 gpu-hours/day per node (single GPU assumption), node_month = 24*30 = 720 node-hours/month
h200_nodes_needed = int(h200_monthly_hours / 720)  # ~224 nodes
```

maya: Good — that node count looks large but helps frame procurement. Procurement: if lead time is 12 weeks, we need POs upstream now to hit late-Oct capacity.

ashley: I'll draft the PO template and run numbers vs committed vs spot for finance. Also adding a short note: consider a 3–6 month stepping plan (phased arrival) to smooth cash.

simon: Re routing + cost: include a metric in the console that shows cost per effective token for each model class so product owners can pick routes based on budget.

maya: Perfect. Let's align in tomorrow's infra sync: procurement + infra + scheduling. If anyone has vendor contacts with earlier H200 windows in APAC, DM me. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Reminder scheduled: infra-sync: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC.

ashley: ack, prepping slides and simple graphs for the sync.

(small thread, short replies after this for follow-ups)
